subject: microbiology
title: Haemophilus, Bordetella and zoonotic bacilli

steps.tx: **Haemophilus influenzae** (tiny coccobacilli needing **X factor hemin and V factor NAD** on chocolate agar, satellites around Staph streaks) splits into **type b Hib** (capsular, epiglottitis with **thumbprint sign**, meningitis under five, septic arthritis) and non typable strains (otitis media, COPD exacerbations, conjunctivitis). **Hib conjugate vaccine** (PRP-T, infants) collapsed invasive disease; treatment is **ceftriaxone** with rifampicin prophylaxis for household contacts. H. ducreyi (chancroid, school of fish, painful soft chancre with bubo) differs genitally.
steps.say: Chocolate agar satellites needing X and V are Haemophilus. Thumbprint airway in a toddler is Hib epiglottitis.

steps.tx: **Bordetella pertussis** (strict aerobe, Bordet-Gengou with mercury drop colonies, pertussis toxin ADP ribosylating Gi with **lymphocytosis**) coughs in three acts: **catarrhal** (coryza, most infectious), **paroxysmal** (whooping inspiratory gasp with posttussive vomiting, 100 day cough), **convalescent**. Infants apnoeic without whoop die fastest; **azithromycin** treats with **cocooning** (vaccinating contacts) protecting neonates. **Acellular DTaP** replaced whole cell DPT for safety; parapertussis runs milder without vaccine cover.
steps.say: Whoop with vomit after cough bursts is pertussis. Lymphocytosis plus 100 days seals it.

steps.tx: **Brucella** (small Gram negative coccobacilli, **undulant fever** rising and falling, farm and abattoir exposure to cattle, goats and pigs, unpasteurised milk) hides intracellularly causing night sweats, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly and sacroiliitis; **doxycycline plus rifampicin or gentamicin** for six weeks prevents relapse. Diagnosis is **standard agglutination with 2 mercaptoethanol** (IgG) and blood or bone marrow culture (Castaneda). B. abortus (cattle), melitensis (goats, commonest and severest) and suis (pigs) sort by host; RB51 vaccinates cattle.
steps.say: Wavy fever with animal contact is brucellosis: doxy plus rifampicin for weeks. Raw milk warns.

steps.tx: **Yersinia pestis** (bipolar safety pin, Wayson stain, rat flea **Xenopsylla cheopis**) causes **bubonic plague** (painful bubo with blackened skin), septicaemic and **pneumonic plague** (person to person, haemoptysis, prophylaxis for contacts). Treatment is **gentamicin or streptomycin plus doxycycline**. **Francisella tularensis** (rabbit fever, ulceroglandular with tick or fly bite) and **Pasteurella multocida** (cat or dog bite rapid cellulitis, penicillin sensitive) complete bite patterns; **Moraxella catarrhalis** (otitis, COPD, beta lactamase positive, butterscotch colonies) rounds respiratory triads.
steps.say: Painful bubo after rat fleas is plague: aminoglycoside fast. Cat bite cellulitis in hours is Pasteurella.
